chunks: And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance; but inevitable is My word that I will fill Hell with jinn and humans all together.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Haqqa al-Qawl' in Surah As-Sajdah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the transition from God's absolute power (Qudrah) to His decisive decree (Al-Qawl) regarding the fulfillment of Hell, emphasizing that guidance is granted but not forced upon every soul. It underscores the principle of divine justice where the 'word' of filling Hell is a settled reality resulting from the free choices of jinn and humans, rather than arbitrary predestination. This reflects the Shia view of 'Amr Bayn al-Amrayn' (a position between absolute predestination and total free will).
